Article Title: Microsoft net income rises 32% to $36.6 billion days after buyout offer to 60,000 staff
Article Text:
Microsoft posts $36.6 billion profit as 60,000 staff offered voluntary exits

Microsoft Cloud revenue rises 30%, Azure grows 48%

Microsoft projects December-quarter revenue of up to $97.1 billion

Capital expenditure expected to exceed $50 billion in December quarter

Microsoft offers voluntary buyouts to around 60,000 employees

Microsoft reported a 32 per cent year-on-year rise in net income to $36.6 billion in the July-September quarter, days after announcing a voluntary buyout offer for around 60,000 employees, more than a quarter of its global workforce.India is among the four countries where the offer applies, alongside the US, Canada and the UK.The technology major began fiscal year 2027 with higher revenue and earnings, supported by strong growth in its cloud business. Revenue for the first quarter ended September 30, 2026, rose 19 per cent to $92.3 billion from $77.7 billion in the corresponding quarter last year. Operating income increased 21 per cent to $45.9 billion.Microsoft's cloud business remained a key contributor to its results, with Microsoft Cloud revenue reaching $63.9 billion, up 30 per cent year-on-year and 31 per cent in constant currency. Azure revenue grew 48 per cent during the quarter.Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella highlighted the performance in a post on X. “Just wrapped our earnings call. It was a fast start to our fiscal year. Microsoft Cloud revenue surpassed $63B, with growth accelerating to 30% YoY,” he said.Revenue from Microsoft's Agents and Infra segment rose 25 per cent to $76.8 billion. The company's commercial remaining performance obligation, which represents contracted revenue yet to be recognised, increased 73 per cent to $677 billion.“We delivered a strong start to the fiscal year with Microsoft Cloud revenue of $63.9 billion, with growth accelerating to 30% (up 31% in constant currency) year-over-year,” said Amy Hood, Microsoft's executive vice president and chief financial officer. She added that the company exceeded expectations across revenue, operating income and earnings per share.Diluted earnings per share increased 32 per cent to $4.92 on a reported basis. Excluding the impact of investments in OpenAI, adjusted net income rose 18 per cent to $36.4 billion, while adjusted earnings per share increased 18 per cent to $4.89.Microsoft expects revenue of $96 billion to $97.1 billion in the December quarter, representing growth of 18-19 per cent. Azure revenue growth is projected at 49-50 per cent in constant currency.Hood said customer demand continues to exceed available supply, while improvements in the efficiency of the company's computing infrastructure are helping it serve more demand.Microsoft's capital expenditure stood at $45.2 billion in the September quarter. Hood expects spending to exceed $50 billion in the December quarter, with capital expenditure for calendar year 2026 projected at approximately $170 billion. The estimate partly reflects capacity deliveries delayed from earlier periods.However, not all business segments recorded growth. Revenue from Microsoft's Devices and Consumer segment declined 3 per cent to $15.5 billion. Windows OEM and devices revenue fell 22 per cent, while Xbox content and services revenue declined 2 per cent. Search and advertising revenue, excluding traffic acquisition costs, grew 12 per cent.The company's financial performance comes as it offers voluntary buyouts to around 60,000 employees, more than a quarter of its global workforce. Chief people officer Amy Coleman announced the Voluntary Exit Offer (VEO) in a memo to staff on Monday, presenting it as an option for employees already considering a future outside Microsoft to leave with financial support and career planning assistance.The terms mirror Microsoft's standard severance arrangements. Eligible employees in the US, Canada, the UK and India at level 70 and below have until the first week of December to decide whether to accept the offer. The level band extends up to general managers and some vice presidents. Employees who accept will leave the company at the end of the year.Unlike the retirement buyout Microsoft offered earlier this year, the VEO has no age or tenure requirement, and performance does not determine eligibility.However, the offer is not available to every employee at level 70 or below. Microsoft has left the decision on participation to individual business leaders. Coleman's memo said participation would depend on each unit's priorities, customer commitments and workforce needs.
Article Summary: Microsoft posts $36.6 billion profit as 60,000 staff offered voluntary exits. Cloud revenue rises 30%, Azure grows 48% in July-September quarter. Microsoft projects December-quarter revenue of up to $97.1 billion.Capital expenditure expected to exceed $50 billion in December quarter.

Article Title: Google parent Alphabet loses $500 billion in market value as AI spending spooks investors
Article Text:
The $500 billion wipeout marked the second-largest single-day loss in market value recorded by a company, after chipmaker Nvidia lost nearly $600 billion in early 2025

AI spending raises questions about returns

Why investors are becoming cautious about AI

Shares of Google parent Alphabet plunged more than 12% on Thursday, wiping out around $500 billion in market value in one of the biggest single-day losses in stock market history. The sell-off reflected growing investor concerns over the company's escalating artificial intelligence spending, slowing growth in its search advertising business and uncertainty over how quickly its investments will generate returns.The decline marked Alphabet's worst single-day fall on record, exceeding its losses during the Covid-19 pandemic and the 2008 financial crisis, according to CNN. The market value erosion was the second-largest single-day loss recorded by a company, after chipmaker Nvidia lost nearly $600 billion in early 2025.The sharp fall followed Alphabet's quarterly earnings report, released on Wednesday, which showed sales below analysts' expectations. Investors were particularly concerned about the outlook for Google's search advertising business, which has long been a major source of revenue and profit.The company is facing growing competition from artificial intelligence-powered chatbots that allow users to seek information without relying on traditional search results. Investors fear this shift could weaken Google's advertising business if consumers increasingly turn to AI tools, including those developed by competitors, to find answers online.The concern is that the transition could happen faster than Google can adapt its business model. Jed Ellerbroek, portfolio manager at Argent Capital Management, told CNN that the displacement of traditional search could happen “faster than Google can react to it and pivot their business.”Alongside concerns about its core search business, Alphabet's rapidly rising expenditure on AI infrastructure has intensified scrutiny of its financial performance.The company reported $51.4 billion in capital expenditure in the third quarter alone, compared with $91.4 billion for the whole of 2025. The spending includes investments in data centres and computing infrastructure needed to develop and operate AI services.While technology companies are pouring hundreds of billions of dollars into infrastructure to compete in the AI race, investors are increasingly questioning whether the spending will translate into sustainable profits.A key concern for Alphabet is its free cash flow, which measures the cash remaining after operating expenses and capital investments. The company recorded negative free cash flow for a second consecutive quarter, according to CNN. Before this year, Google had not reported a negative figure for any quarter since going public in 2004.Negative free cash flow does not necessarily indicate that a company is unprofitable. However, it means less cash is available after investment spending to fund shareholder returns, including dividends and share buybacks, or to support other business priorities.Alphabet's performance stood in contrast to Microsoft, which reported $18.6 billion in free cash flow for the third quarter despite continuing to invest heavily in AI infrastructure. Microsoft's shares ended Thursday's session largely unchanged, while Alphabet suffered a double-digit decline.“We are now getting to see who is spending rationally on AI and who is not,” Richard Reyle, chief investment officer at Questar Capital Partners, told CNN.The sell-off highlights a broader shift in how markets are evaluating the AI boom. Investors are no longer looking only at the scale of companies' investments or the growth potential of the technology. They are also assessing whether those investments can generate adequate returns, how much cash they consume and whether AI could undermine existing revenue streams.Alphabet is attempting to expand its AI capabilities while defending its dominant search business. Its investments could help it compete in a rapidly changing technology market, but the returns remain uncertain as the industry races to build data centres and secure computing capacity.Even the prospect of future demand from AI companies does not guarantee immediate profitability. Although AI firms are committing to large amounts of computing power, the financial benefits depend on whether demand continues to grow and whether the infrastructure can be monetised at a sufficient scale.Technology companies are also increasingly turning to debt and financial markets to fund their ambitions, raising questions about the sustainability of the industry's capital spending.“Everybody is trying to get through the door at the same time, and it gives people pause,” Ted Mortonson, a technology-focused investment strategist at Baird, told CNN.For Alphabet, the challenge is to demonstrate that its massive AI investments can produce profitable growth without weakening the cash-generating search business that has supported the company for years. Thursday's steep decline suggests investors are demanding clearer evidence of those returns rather than accepting spending growth as a sign of future success.
Article Summary: Shares of Google parent Alphabet plunged more than 12% on Thursday, wiping out around $500 billion in market value. The sell-off reflected growing investor concerns over the company's escalating artificial intelligence spending, slowing growth in its search advertising business and uncertainty over how quickly its investments will generate returns. The decline marked Alphabet's worst single- day fall on record.

Article Title: Amazon shares sink 7% as AI spending fuels cash-burn concerns, overshadow cloud growth
Article Text:
Amazon cloud business accelerates but shares drop on profit miss

Cash burn and outlook weigh on sentiment

Advertising business misses expectations

AI spending pressures spread across Big Tech

Amazon shares fell sharply in after-hours trading on Thursday (local time) as heavy artificial intelligence investments and a weaker-than-expected earnings performance overshadowed accelerating growth in its cloud computing business.The e-commerce and technology giant’s shares dropped as much as 7% after it reported third-quarter results that missed Wall Street expectations and issued a cautious revenue outlook for the crucial holiday shopping quarter. The stock had already fallen 4.3% during regular trading to close at $243.79.Amazon’s cloud computing unit, Amazon Web Services (AWS), delivered a standout performance, with revenue rising 39% year-on-year to $46 billion in the quarter ended September 30. This marked its fastest growth in nearly five years and accelerated from the 37% increase recorded in the previous quarter. Revenue also exceeded analysts’ expectations of $45.61 billion, according to LSEG data.However, investors remained concerned about the cost of expanding the business to capitalise on growing demand for artificial intelligence. Amazon has forecast capital expenditure of $220 billion for 2026, largely to build AI data centres and expand its technology infrastructure.Chief executive Andy Jassy told analysts that capital expenditure would be “meaningfully more” next year, without providing a specific figure. “Our strategy is working and I expect it will for the foreseeable future,” Jassy said, defending the company’s investment plans.He also said AWS could become a business generating more than $1 trillion in annual revenue within five to 10 years, adding that demand for the unit’s services remained strong.“Customers are gobbling it up,” Jassy said, referring to the rapid adoption of Amazon’s AI infrastructure.Amazon’s spending plans have raised questions about how quickly its AI investments will translate into stronger cash generation. The company reported a trailing 12-month cash burn of $42.4 billion in the September quarter, driven by heavy capital expenditure. Spending on capital projects during the quarter reached $77.26 billion, around $20 billion above estimates compiled by LSEG.“The free cash flow looks like the ugly part of the report,” said Dave Wagner, portfolio manager at Aptus Capital Advisors. “Operations generated plenty of cash but their capex just absolutely swallowed it.”Amazon reported net sales of $201.94 billion for the quarter, up 12% from $180.17 billion a year earlier. Net income declined to $20.69 billion, or $1.89 per share, from $21.19 billion, or $1.95 per share, in the year-ago period. Analysts had expected earnings of $1.97 per share on revenue of $202.2 billion, according to FactSet.The company forecast fourth-quarter net sales of between $240 billion and $247 billion, representing growth of 12% to 16% from a year earlier. The midpoint of the range, $243.5 billion, was slightly below analysts’ estimate of $244.51 billion, according to LSEG.The outlook covers the holiday shopping season, a crucial period for Amazon’s retail business, as consumers contend with elevated living costs and higher fuel prices.Amazon’s advertising division also disappointed investors. Revenue rose 12 per cent to $19.6 billion, falling short of analysts’ expectations for growth of 18%. It was the first time in seven quarters that the business missed estimates, according to Reuters.The slowdown contrasted with growth of 26% in the previous quarter and 22% in the year-ago period. Jassy attributed some of the weakness to the timing of the company’s Prime Day shopping event, which took place in the second quarter this year in most major markets, including the US.Amazon said the shift in Prime Day’s timing also affected its overall third-quarter sales growth. Excluding the calendar change, year-on-year revenue growth would have been approximately four percentage points higher, the company said.Amazon’s results come amid growing investor scrutiny of the enormous sums technology companies are committing to AI infrastructure and whether the spending will deliver adequate returns.Alphabet, the parent company of Google and YouTube, saw its shares plunge 12% on Thursday after investors reacted to its latest results and rising expenditure on property and equipment. Microsoft, meanwhile, lowered its capital expenditure outlook to $170 billion from $175 billion.The sell-off reflects concerns that the race to build data centres and deploy AI chips could strain cash flows even at some of the industry’s largest companies.Amazon is also facing scrutiny over the impact of its expanding data centre footprint on local communities. Earlier this month, the company said it would invest more than $1 billion over five years in communities where it operates data centres, including funding for education, job training, water conservation and energy-related initiatives.Despite the concerns, Amazon continues to expand its retail operations through faster deliveries, automation and AI-powered warehouse technology. Jassy has argued that these investments are strengthening the company’s competitive position, while the latest AWS results indicate that demand for its cloud infrastructure remains robust.
Article Summary: Amazon shares fell sharply in after-hours trading on Thursday (local time) as heavy artificial intelligence investments and a weaker-than-expected earnings performance overshadowed accelerating growth in its cloud computing business. The e-commerce and technology giant’s shares dropped as much as 7% after it reported third-quarter results that missed Wall Street expectations.

Article Title: 3 Wall Street firms agree to pay up to $100,000 a month to get Trump’s posts faster: How it works
Article Text:
3 trading firms agree to pay Trump’s Truth Social for faster access

How Truth API works

Who is paying for the service?

Why the paid feed has drawn criticism

Trump Media’s financial portfolio

US President Donald Trump’s paid social media service, Truth API, has found customers, with Bloomberg and two high-frequency trading firms paying for faster access to his posts. The service costs financial institutions up to $100,000 a month.Two sources with direct knowledge of the matter, cited by Reuters, said Susquehanna International Group and Jump Trading, both of which specialise in algorithmic and automated trading strategies, have also signed up for the service.The deals give subscribers a timing advantage over people who monitor Trump’s posts on the app themselves.The arrangement has raised concerns about the sale of faster access to statements by a sitting president, particularly because his posts can influence financial markets.It also comes as Trump Media and Technology Group, the company behind Truth Social, faces legal challenges over the paid service and questions about the potential use of presidential communications for commercial gain.Trump Media and Technology Group announced the faster-access product in July, pitching it to trading firms and other financial institutions. The service is designed to deliver Trump’s posts more quickly than a person could obtain them by repeatedly checking Truth Social.Trump Media officials have put the timing advantage at 50 milliseconds. For financial firms using automated trading systems, that difference can matter when a presidential statement triggers a change in asset prices.High-frequency traders rely on software to scan news headlines, company announcements and government statements for information that could move markets. Their systems can read and analyse the information before executing trades in thousandths of a second.The potential consequences of Trump’s social media posts were evident in April, when oil futures fell after he announced a ceasefire in the Iran war on Truth Social.An application programming interface, or API, acts as a digital bridge that allows one computer system to communicate with another. In this case, the product gives subscribers faster access to the president’s posts, which they can use in their trading or financial information systems.According to a Reuters report, Bloomberg, Susquehanna International Group and Jump Trading are among the organisations that have signed up for Truth API.In August, Trump Media told investors it had "signed more than 10 customer agreements”. Reuters was unable to independently confirm that figure.The company did not identify its customers but said they were primarily Wall Street trading firms paying between $60,000 and $100,000 a month. The latest deals indicate that the product has attracted both financial trading firms and a news and data provider.Reuters, which competes with Bloomberg in financial news, said in a statement: "We will assess the service, but have no current plans to subscribe."Trump Media defended the product in a statement, saying: “Truth Social offers an industry-standard API product for which there is significant demand across industries. We take customer confidentiality seriously. This reporting is based on misleading information being peddled by anonymous sources aimed at harming our company, customers and shareholders.”The company has not publicly named the subscribers in its August investor update, and the three firms named in the report declined to comment.The paid service has drawn criticism for giving subscribers faster access to a president’s statements, potentially offering financial firms an advantage when his posts move markets. The deals are likely the first time a business linked to a sitting president has sold access to his statements.In July, Democratic Senators Elizabeth Warren of Massachusetts and Adam Schiff of California asked the US Securities and Exchange Commission to investigate whether the service violated securities laws. They called it a “shocking abuse” of office by a president seeking personal gain.A Trump Media and Technology Group spokesperson said, “Congressional Democrats continue to mischaracterize Truth API either out of ideological opposition to free markets or a failure to grasp the distinction between public and nonpublic information.”In August, Intercept Media and the non-profit Freedom of the Press Foundation sued Trump, seeking to stop the White House from posting official government announcements exclusively on Truth Social. The ongoing lawsuit describes the service as "profoundly corrupt" and alleges violations of the First and Fifth Amendments.The commercial arrangement has also drawn attention to the ownership of Trump Media. The president’s family trust owns 41% of the company, and Trump is the trust’s sole beneficiary.The Truth API deals come as Trump Media faces a steep decline in its stock market value.Shares of the company have fallen more than 50% so far this year. Its market value has also been volatile since it went public in March 2024.The company closed at a market value of about $8 billion on its debut in March 2024, but is now worth about $1.8 billion.Since 2024, Trump Media has lost about $1.76 billion, including non-cash charges.
Article Summary: Bloomberg, Susquehanna International Group and Jump Trading are among the organisations that have signed up for Truth API. The service is designed to deliver Trump’s posts more quickly than a person could obtain them by repeatedly checking Truth Social. For financial firms using automated trading systems, that difference can matter when a presidential statement triggers a change in asset prices.

Article Title: Oil prices rise as Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia stoke supply fears; Brent nears $116
Article Text:
Brent futures gained 86 cents, or 0.75%, to $115.74 a barrel

Peace overtures fail to ease tensions

Crude oil prices continued their upward march on Friday, with Brent crossing $115 a barrel as attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure and mounting risks to shipping in the Gulf heightened fears of supply disruptions. The benchmarks were also heading for their fourth consecutive monthly rise, with US crude poised to settle above $100 for the first time since April.Brent futures gained 86 cents, or 0.75 per cent, to $115.74 a barrel by 0122 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) rose 72 cents, or 0.71 per cent, to $102.72.Brent was on course for a nearly 14 per cent gain in October, while WTI was set to jump around 15 per cent. Both were heading for their sharpest monthly increases since July.The latest escalation came on Thursday, when Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthi group claimed attacks on key Saudi oil installations, including the Ras Tanura and Rabigh refineries and an Aramco facility in Abqaiq. A Saudi-led coalition separately reported intercepting a cruise missile launched towards the kingdom’s western region.The developments have heightened concerns over the security of energy infrastructure and shipping routes at a time when prospects for a diplomatic breakthrough remain uncertain.“Continued kinetic action around the Strait of Hormuz amidst doubts of a viable diplomatic pathway are keeping oil prices elevated in expectation of an escalation of the conflict in coming weeks,” said Saul Kavonic, head of energy research at MST Marquee.The Strait of Hormuz remains a major source of concern for energy markets, with any disruption to traffic through the waterway threatening to constrain global oil supplies.Efforts to reopen diplomatic channels between Washington and Tehran have yet to provide markets with reassurance.US President Donald Trump said on Thursday that Vice President JD Vance had contacted Iran to help it obtain medical supplies. This followed US media reports that Vance had written to Iran’s top security official in a bid to restart peace negotiations.Iran has received the letter but has not responded, the semi-official Tasnim news agency reported. Tehran is insisting that Washington accept its conditions, the agency said, quoting the Iranian position that “any position that contradicts this framework is unacceptable.”At sea, Iran’s Revolutionary Guards reported that three tankers had hit sea mines, exploded and caught fire while attempting to use an unauthorised route south of the Strait of Hormuz. The report added to the security concerns surrounding maritime traffic in the region.The heightened risks are also prompting changes to corporate travel plans. ExxonMobil and Chevron have cancelled plans for their executives to attend the United Arab Emirates’ biggest oil show next week, two sources familiar with the matter told Reuters.With crude prices already recording substantial monthly gains, traders are watching for signs that the conflict could further disrupt oil production or transportation. The trajectory of diplomatic efforts and the security of key energy routes are likely to remain central to market sentiment.
Article Summary: Brent futures gained 86 cents, or 0.75%, to $115.74 a barrel. US crude poised to settle above $100 for the first time since April. Attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure and mounting risks to shipping in the Gulf have heightened fears of supply disruptions.

Article Title: Sebi relaxes timeline for FPI KYC updates
Article Text:
Sebi extends FPI KYC review timelines from one to two years and three to eight years to ease compliance, while retaining the 10-year cycle for Swagat-FIs

MUMBAI: To simplify the compliance process for foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) registered in India, markets regulator Sebi on Friday extended the periodicity of Know Your Client (KYC) review from one year at present to eight years."Currently, FPIs are subject to periodic KYC review annually or once every three years, depending on the applicable category and other criteria. The revised framework increases the periodicity from one year to two years and from three years to eight years," a Sebi circular said. For some special category of FPI labelled under Swagat-FIs, "the periodicity of KYC review will remain unchanged at 10 years. Also, the existing relaxations for GS-FPIs will remain unchanged," the circular said.
Article Summary: Sebi extends periodicity of Know Your Client (KYC) review from one year to eight years. Currently, FPIs are subject to periodic KYC review annually or once every three years. For some special category of FPI labelled under Swagat-FIs, periodicity will remain unchanged at 10 years.

Article Title: Nasdaq bleeds: Faces $2 trillion wipeout in October
Article Text:
Nasdaq bleeds: Faces $2 trillion wipeout in October

Nasdaq 100 set to lose over $2 trillion in October as rising AI spending fuels investor concerns

More than $2 trillion in market value is set to be wiped from the tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 this month, as Big Tech earnings intensified investor scrutiny of whether the billions being poured into artificial intelligence can generate returns quickly enough.The wipeout would amount to slightly more than SpaceX's entire market value. The index has fallen over 5.8% so far in Oct as the AI trade ran into turbulence, with hyperscalers Meta Platforms, Alphabet and Amazon.com raising spending forecasts further as they race to expand AI infrastructure.The prospect of ever-bigger AI outlays has unnerved investors, particularly as rising borrowing costs threaten to make debt-funded investment more expensive and harder to justify.Alphabet suffered its biggest one-day percentage drop on record on Thursday after disappointing results in the core business of search advertising and a massive acceleration in cash burn. Meta's plans for a record $97.5 billion fund raise heightened concerns about shareholder dilution and whether mounting AI spending could force other Big Tech companies to increasingly tap capital markets.On Friday, Intel's stock led the way lower and was flirting with its worst day since 1974 after tumbling 30%.Microsoft and SpaceX broke from the gloom, with results that showed AI spending starting to pay off."It may be that we've overestimated how strong the growth might be, but they're not going negative in aggregate," said John Bilton, global head of strategic research at Multi-Asset Solutions."We have an insatiable and growing demand for data." Microsoft is reportedly planning to raise about $25 billion through its first US investment-grade bond sale in more than nine years. Among other hyperscalers, Meta, Amazon and Alphabet have issued hundreds of billions of dollars in bond sales over the past four years, worrying investors about overreliance on the medium for raising capital. Morgan Stanley forecast capital spending on AI infrastructure overall will surpass a trillion dollars next year. AI companies' growing reliance on debt funding is emerging as a new risk for investors, challenging the view that the companies at the heart of the boom are insulated from macroeconomic pressures.The concern is spreading beyond stocks to credit markets, where investors are starting to price in the possibility that rising financing costs, combined with slower returns on AI spending, could squeeze companies previously viewed as relatively insulated. Revenue across the "Magnificent Seven" has remained strong since ChatGPT's launch in 2022, showcasing insatiable demand and perhaps why investors were initially willing to back the spending, even as the timeline of payoffs remains uncertain.Amazon's cloud computing cash cow, Amazon Web Services, continued to accelerate, while Meta offered better-than-expected revenue growth and an upbeat outlook. Microsoft also forecast strong cloud growth in its latest earnings report.Big Tech has historically spent heavily on infrastructure to build and expand businesses such as cloud computing, online advertising and e-commerce, but the AI boom has pushed capital expenditure to dizzying levels. JP Morgan expects global AI capex to reach $5.5 trillion by 2030, and sees $900 billion being spent in 2026 alone. Reuters
Article Summary: Nasdaq 100 set to lose over $2 trillion in October as rising AI spending fuels investor concerns. The wipeout would amount to slightly more than SpaceX's entire market value. The index has fallen over 5.8% so far in Oct as the AI trade ran into turbulence.

Article Title: US midterm elections: What a Democratic win could mean for India's trade
Article Text:
US midterms may raise shutdown, keep tariff uncertainty high

Tariff uncertainty to continue - Here’s why

AI, data centres unlikely to face a major investment shift

The US is preparing for its November 3 midterm elections, but the results will be closely watched in India too, particularly for their possible impact on trade ties and business conditions.The outcome could bring fresh uncertainty around US trade policies, with tariffs, government spending and the risk of a government shutdown among the key issues.For India, a change in the political balance in Washington could mean greater scrutiny of President Donald Trump's policies, but businesses may not get an immediate relief from the existing tariff framework.A major shift in Trump's policy direction remains unlikely, according to a report by ICICI Bank. The report estimates that Democrats have a 63 per cent probability of gaining control of both chambers of Congress. Their chances of winning the House of Representatives stand at 90.9 per cent, while the probability of securing the Senate is 64 per cent.A Democratic sweep could bring the Trump administration's policies on tariffs, immigration and government spending under greater scrutiny. However, a change in congressional control may not necessarily lead to an immediate change in the policies currently in place.A change in congressional control may bring more debate around US trade policies, but businesses should not expect the current tariff framework to disappear overnight."The more immediate effects of Democratic control would likely be increased oversight, legislative disputes and greater uncertainty for businesses, rather than an automatic dismantling of the current tariff framework," the report said.Democrats could push for a review of certain tariffs or attempt to restrict the President's powers to impose them. However, any significant change could face hurdles, as the US President retains the power to veto legislation and has certain independent powers to impose tariffs.For India, this means that uncertainty around the US trade and tariff approach could remain even if Democrats make gains in Congress.A change in the political balance alone may not bring an immediate shift in the administration's policy direction.The report does not expect the midterm election results to significantly alter investments in artificial intelligence (AI) and data centres in the US.“The toss-up states where Republicans can lose in the midterm collectively account for only ~15% of total data center capacity in the US”, the report said.This limits the extent to which a change in political control could affect the sector's investment landscape. However, data centres could face greater scrutiny over their resource consumption and environmental impact.Democrats have raised concerns about the high electricity and water requirements of these facilities. An average data centre with a capacity of 100 megawatts consumes around 2 million litres of water daily and uses more electricity than 75,000 homes, according to the report.The sector could also face closer examination over its environmental impact and effect on employment. The report has also flagged the possibility of a fresh dispute over the US debt ceiling in mid-2027.The debt ceiling is the legal limit on how much the federal government can borrow. US government debt stood at around $40 trillion in late 2026, against a borrowing limit of $41.1 trillion.
Article Summary: US midterms could bring fresh uncertainty around US trade policies, with tariffs, government spending and the risk of a government shutdown among the key issues. ICICI Bank estimates that Democrats have a 63 per cent probability of gaining control of both chambers of Congress. However, a change in congressional control may not necessarily lead to an immediate change in the policies.

Article Title: NBFCs overtake housing as biggest driver of bank credit
Article Text:
Banks add Rs 16.1 lakh crore in non-food credit in H1 FY27, with NBFCs, industry and personal loans driving growth; lending to NBFCs rises by Rs 1.8 lakh crore

Clooneys' foundation gives free legal aid to over 9,000 women and children

MUMBAI: Banks lent more to NBFCs than to home buyers in the first half of FY27, with advances to non-bank lenders rising by Rs 1.8 lakh crore, compared with Rs 1.4 lakh crore for housing. Of the Rs 16.1 lakh crore incremental non-food credit added between March 31 and Sept 30, industry accounted for Rs 3.7 lakh crore, while trade absorbed Rs 1 lakh crore, reflecting strong demand across corporate and services segments.Scheduled commercial banks' outstanding non-food credit rose 19.1% year on year to Rs 229 lakh crore at the end of Sept, with the six-month expansion marking a 7.5% increase over March. Services accounted for the largest share of incremental lending at Rs 4.9 lakh crore, followed by personal loans at Rs 4.5 lakh crore, industry at Rs 3.7 lakh crore and agriculture at Rs 1.8 lakh crore.Gold loans continued to be a major contributor to retail credit growth. Outstanding advances against gold jewellery surged 82.6% year-on-year to Rs 5.8 lakh crore, rising 25.1% in the first half alone. Banks added Rs 1.2 lakh crore in gold loans between March and Sept.Within services, lending to NBFCs grew 41.8% year-on-year to Rs 22.5 lakh crore. Commercial real estate advances rose 23.3% to Rs 7.5 lakh crore, while trade credit grew 23.9%. Services credit as a whole expanded 28.3% to Rs 64.9 lakh crore, accounting for 30.6% of incremental non-food lending.Industrial credit grew 19.5% to Rs 49.8 lakh crore. While advances to large industries rose 16% to Rs 33 lakh crore, lending to medium enterprises grew 33.2% and to micro and small enterprises 24.4%. Of the Rs 3.7 lakh crore incremental industrial credit, large companies accounted for Rs 2 lakh crore and MSMEs Rs 1.6 lakh crore.Agriculture and allied activities credit rose 19.5% to Rs 28.2 lakh crore from Rs 23.6 lakh crore a year earlier. Personal loans grew 17.3% to Rs 74.27 lakh crore, although the composition of retail lending shifted towards secured advances.One of the fastest-growing segments was loans against fixed deposits, including FCNR(B) and NRNR deposits. Outstanding advances in this category rose 53.3% year-on-year to Rs 2.2 lakh crore, increasing 28.1% in the six months to Sept. Banks added Rs 47,471 crore in such loans during the period.These advances accounted for 10.6% of the Rs 4.5 lakh crore incremental personal loans during the half-year and 3% of the banking system's incremental non-food credit.
Article Summary: Banks lent more to NBFCs than to home buyers in the first half of FY27. Outstanding non-food credit rose 19.1% year on year to Rs 229 lakh crore at the end of Sept. Services accounted for the largest share of incremental lending at Rs 4.9 lakh crore.

Article Title: Power, fertiliser fuel LNG import surge
Article Text:
LNG imports hit a record 2.7 million tonnes in October, rising 17.4% on higher demand and a rebound in supplies from Qatar.

Crude imports also touch a record 5.6 million barrels per day in October, with Russia retaining its position as the top supplier despite declining shipments.

NEW DELHI: India's LNG imports rose 17.4% to a record 2.7 million tonnes so far in Oct on the back of higher demand from the power, fertiliser and city gas distribution sectors. Besides, more cargo arrived from Qatar and the UAE, data from maritime intelligence and research firm Kpler showed.Crude imports also reached a record 5.6 million barrels per day (mbd) during the month, 14% higher than a year ago, with Russia remaining the top supplier, while shipments from West Asia and the Atlantic Basin also rose.LNG supplies increased as India's domestic production has declined, pushing up the import dependence from 50% to nearly 52%. In addition, companies are seen to be stocking up the gas for the power sector, as solar energy is set to decline in winters, and the fertiliser sector will need higher feedstock for production.According to Kpler data, the record LNG imports in Oct can be attributed to a sharp rebound in supplies from Qatar, which had remained curtailed due to disruptions in shipments through the Strait of Hormuz during the West Asia conflict. Qatar has traditionally been the biggest supplier of LNG to India, accounting for 40-50% of total imported volumes. In Sept last year, India imported nearly 2.1 MT of LNG, of which 0.8 MT came from Qatar.India received more than 0.4 MT of LNG from Qatar this month, the highest volume since the war broke out. The supplies were 370% more than the 0.1 MT received from the West Asian nation in Sept, and only marginally lower than the cumulative imports between March and Sept.Despite its production facilities being impacted, sources said Qatar was willing to increase LNG supplies and meet its long-term commitments to customers.The US, however, continued to remain the biggest supplier of LNG, with 0.6 MT of supplies till Oct 29. The UAE, Oman, Angola, Nigeria and Australia were other major suppliers during the month. Though Russian crude flows have declined from a peak of 2.8 mbd in July to nearly 2 mbd in Oct, Moscow remained the largest supplier, accounting for nearly 36% of total imports.Nikhil Dubey, Kpler's lead analyst - refining, however, said elevated freight costs of Russian barrels had eroded their delivered-price advantage, while improved supplies from West Asia offered competitive alternatives to refiners. He said supplies from Gulf countries stood at around 2.3 mbd in Oct, compared with 2.7 mbd in Sept, with Saudi Arabia leading the pack, followed by Iraq.
Article Summary: India's LNG imports hit a record 2.7 million tonnes in October, rising 17.4% on higher demand and a rebound in supplies from Qatar. Crude imports also touch a record 5.6 million barrels per day, with Russia retaining its position as the top supplier.

Article Title: 'Play only administrative role in NCLT appointment'
Article Text:
MCA says its role in appointing NCLT members is only administrative, a day after the Supreme Court accused the ministry of “completely hijacking” the tribunals

NEW DELHI: A day after Supreme Court's observation on the role of ministry of corporate affairs in the appointment and infrastructure in the National Company Law Tribunal and the appellate tribunal, the ministry on Friday said it only performed "administrative" role in conducting the appointment process for the 63 judicial and technical members of the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT)"NCLT independently undertakes the process for appointment and management of its officers and staff, including deputy registrars, court officers, stenographers, office assistants and multi-tasking staff," MCA said in a statement.In Oct 2019, govt delegated the responsibility to NCLT to ensure its effective and independent functioning, govt added. On Thursday, SC slammed the ministry for "completely hijacking" both NCLT and NCLAT, while hearing a petition regarding the dilapidated infrastructure, lack of support staff and vacancies, hampering the work in the tribunal that deals with corporate law and insolvency cases.
Article Summary: MCA says its role in appointing NCLT members is only administrative. Supreme Court accused the ministry of “completely hijacking’ the tribunals on Thursday. In Oct 2019, govt delegated the responsibility to NclT to ensure its effective and independent functioning.

Article Title: AU Bank probes potential data leak
Article Text:
AU Small Finance Bank probes alleged data leak involving a Salesforce-hosted platform holding limited vehicle loan customer information, while saying its core systems remain unaffected

MUMBAI: AU Small Finance Bank is investigating a potential data leak involving a Salesforce-hosted software platform that holds limited information relating to its vehicle loan customers, after a cyber threat intelligence platform flagged claims by a hacking group that it had breached the lender's systems. The bank said the incident involved a software-as-a-service (SaaS) platform managed and hosted by Salesforce."We reaffirm that the Bank's own systems remain unaffected and all banking services are operating normally," a bank spokesperson said. HackRisk.io, a threat intelligence and cyber-attack monitoring platform, flagged the alleged breach in a post on X on Oct 29. The ScarlettGroup hacking group claimed to have accessed sensitive customer and internal corporate data and threatened to release it. According to hackers' claims, the compromised information includes KYC records.
Article Summary: AU Small Finance Bank is investigating a potential data leak involving a Salesforce-hosted software platform. A cyber threat intelligence platform flagged claims by a hacking group that it had breached the lender's systems. The ScarlettGroup hacking group claimed to have accessed sensitive customer and internal corporate data. According to hackers' claims, the compromised information includes KYC records.

Article Title: Trai proposes draft framework for responsible use of AI in tele networks
Article Text:
Trai proposes AI rules for telecom firms, including board-approved policies, safety committees and mandatory reporting of serious AI-related incidents

NEW DELHI: Trai on Friday proposed a comprehensive draft framework for the responsible use of artificial intelligence in telecom networks that would require service providers to adopt board-approved AI policies, establish dedicated governance and safety committees, and report serious AI-related incidents to the regulator.The draft guidelines, released for stakeholder consultations, also seek to make entities accountable for the outcomes of AI systems deployed in their networks and services, "irrespective of whether AI systems are developed internally, procured/ outsourced from a third party or a combination thereof." Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (Trai), in a release, said it has floated the "draft 'Guidelines on Responsible Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Telecommunication Networks and Provision of Telecommunication Services' for stakeholders' comments". Agencies
Article Summary: Trai proposes a comprehensive draft framework for the responsible use of artificial intelligence in telecom networks. Service providers would have to adopt board-approved AI policies, establish dedicated governance and safety committees, and report serious AI-related incidents to the regulator. The draft guidelines also seek to make entities accountable for the outcomes of AI systems deployed in their networks and services.

Article Title: Govt sets up committee to reform banking sector
Article Text:
Centre sets up Suresh N Patel-led panel to recommend comprehensive banking reforms within six months

NEW DELHI: Govt Friday set up a high-level committee under former central vigilance commissioner Suresh N. Patel to undertake comprehensive banking reforms, delivering on an announcement made by finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman in Union budget 2026-27.The five-member panel, which includes RBI deputy governor Shirish Chandra Murmu, former RBI deputy governor N S Vishwanathan, former Indian Bank MD & CEO Padmaja Chunduru alongwith a finance ministry representative, has a tenure of six months to submit a roadmap aimed at reforms necessary to make Indian banking "globally competitive, financially inclusive, and resilient for Viksit Bharat, 2047," said govt.The panel's mandate spans "structural, institutional, regulatory, and legislative" overhauls across commercial banks, regional rural banks (RRBs), cooperative institutions, and non-banking financial companies (NBFCs). Besides assessing long-term capital needs for banks and development financial institutions (DFIs) to spur private investment, the committee will evaluate priority sector lending norms, cybersecurity frameworks, AI adoption, and talent acquisition strategies.This step marks the latest major structural review of the banking sector after Narasimham committee (1998) laid the foundation for tightening capital adequacy ratios and non-performing asset (NPA) norms, in the wake of 1991 liberalisation reforms.Later, Raghuram Rajan committee (2008) advocated incremental structural shifts to expand credit access and financial markets, while Urjit Patel Committee (2014) advocated for inflation targeting by setting up the monetary policy committee.
Article Summary: The panel's mandate spans "structural, institutional, regulatory, and legislative" overhauls across commercial banks, regional rural banks (RRBs), cooperative institutions, and non-banking financial companies (NBFCs) Besides assessing long-term capital needs for banks, the committee will evaluate priority sector lending norms, cybersecurity frameworks, AI adoption, and talent acquisition strategies.

Article Title: Reliance Industries Q2 net rises 34% to Rs 29,550 crore
Article Text:
Reliance Industries reports 34% jump in Q2 profit to Rs 29,550 crore, beating estimates, on strong O2C and Jio performance; revenue rises 29%

Mukesh Ambani-led Reliance posts 34% growth in Q2 profit, with revenue crossing Rs 3.3 lakh crore; board approves Rs 15,000 crore fundraising plan

MUMBAI: Reliance Industries, India's most valuable company by market capitalisation, reported a 34% rise in second-quarter profit for FY27 to Rs 29,550 crore on Friday, beating analysts' average estimate of Rs 21,419 crore. The increase was driven by strong performance at its oil-to-chemicals (O2C) and Jio digital services businesses. Revenue increased 29% to over Rs 3.3 lakh crore, while ebitda climbed 26% to Rs 61,224 crore. Expenses rose 28% to Rs 3 lakh crore.RIL CMD Mukesh Ambani said the O2C business delivered a particularly strong performance in the quarter, led by tight fuel markets, improved petrochemical margins and firm domestic demand.Ebitda at the O2C division, which accounted for 41% of total operating profit, jumped 68% year-on-year to Rs 25,203 crore. Stronger transportation fuel and downstream margins drove the gain.Jio Platforms, which made a blockbuster stock market debut this week, posted an 18% rise in ebitda to Rs 22,223 crore on strong revenue growth, operating leverage and a 250-basis-point margin expansion. Average revenue per user rose nearly 4% to Rs 219, helped by a better subscriber mix and increased usage, partly offset by broadband promotions.Ebitda at the retail unit fell 10% to Rs 6,120 crore, even as revenue grew 6% to Rs 80,220 crore in the second quarter of FY27. RIL said performance was affected by the shift in the festive calendar to the third quarter.Ebitda at the oil and gas division slipped 2% to Rs 4,901 crore due to lower revenue and higher govt levies. Ebitda from smaller businesses, including media and consumer products, was flat at Rs 2,777 crore.RIL had a cash balance of over Rs 2.6 lakh crore, comfortably covering net debt of Rs 1.2 lakh crore. Capital expenditure totalled Rs 38,153 crore, largely driven by investments in O2C and new energy projects, and by the expansion of infrastructure and distribution networks of its consumer businesses.The RIL board on Friday approved a plan to raise Rs 15,000 crore through listed, redeemable non-convertible debentures."This week marked a historic moment in Reliance's value creation journey with Jio's record-setting listing on Indian bourses. It demonstrates the depth of confidence investors place in Jio's solid foundation and strong growth visibility."I am proud to witness the rejuvenation of "the equity cult" originally pioneered by our founder-chairman during the 1977 Reliance IPO," said RIL chairman Mukesh Ambani.
Article Summary: Mukesh Ambani-led Reliance posts 34% growth in Q2 profit, with revenue crossing Rs 3.3 lakh crore. Ebitda at the O2C division, which accounted for 41% of total operating profit, jumped 68% year-on-year.

Article Title: IOC profit surges 2.7x in Q2 on crude price decline
Article Text:
Indian Oil posts record Rs 22,503 crore Q2 profit, 2.7 times higher year-on-year, as lower crude prices and strong petrochemical and gas margins boost earnings

NEW DELHI: State-run Indian Oil Corporation (IOC) reported record profit of Rs 22,503 crore during the Sept quarter - a 2.7-fold jump over a year ago - driven largely by a decline in crude oil prices between July and mid-Aug and robust margins from the petrochemical and gas segments. In the June quarter, the company had reported a loss of Rs 1,241 crore due to elevated crude prices amid the West Asia war. IndianOil, however, warned that profitability in the upcoming quarters may again be impacted by inventory losses if crude oil prices fall with the normalisation of the situation in West Asia.The company's consolidated revenue from operations rose 30% to Rs 2.7 lakh crore in Q2FY27, from Rs 2.1 lakh crore in Q2FY26. For the first half of FY27, IOC reported a consolidated net profit of Rs 21,361.5 crore, up 42% from Rs 14,999 crore in April-Sept FY26.
Article Summary: Indian Oil posts record Rs 22,503 crore Q2 profit, 2.7 times higher year-on- year. Lower crude prices and strong petrochemical and gas margins boost earnings. In June quarter, the company had reported a loss of Rs 1,241 crore due to elevated crude prices.

Article Title: NHAI’s free-flow tolling push to cut land acquisition needs, cap toll plaza lanes at 8
Article Text:
NHAI caps toll plazas on future national highway projects at eight lanes, with MLFF tolling aimed at reducing land acquisition and public spending

New Delhi: All future national highway projects, including those where construction is yet to begin, will have toll plazas with not more than eight lanes, as NHAI has made Multi-Lane Free Flow (MLFF) tolling an integral part of highway development. The move will reduce land acquisition requirements and save public money, as electronic toll collection equipment will be mounted on overhead gantries instead of requiring multiple tolling lanes and booths.At present, several toll plazas on six- and eight-lane highways, particularly around major cities, have over 20 lanes and in some cases this goes up to 32 lanes. In conventional tolling systems, more tolling lanes were required to clear vehicles queuing up at toll gates.“For all practical reasons, there will be no need to acquire any extra land for toll plazas. The tolling system using gantry-mounted high-performance RFID readers and Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) cameras to identify vehicles in motion and deduct the applicable toll through FASTag will be installed on the highway,” said an official.The revised design seeks to rationalise the number of tolling lanes by increasing the vehicle-handling capacity of each lane.NHAI has estimated the throughput of each lane at 600 vehicles per hour while prescribing the new configuration. An additional over-dimension or spare lane will also be provided to handle emergencies.The circular also lays down safety and infrastructure requirements, including a minimum six-metre clearance for gantry-mounted equipment, advance signage, variable message signs around one-km before the plaza and adequate high-mast lighting. Toll plazas will, wherever feasible, be located on straight stretches of highways.The policy will apply to highway projects at different stages of construction. Projects still under the detailed project report (DPR) stage will incorporate the new layout in their bidding documents. For projects already awarded or under construction where toll plaza construction has not started, the revised design will be adopted through changes in the scope of work.NHAI has directed all regional officers, project implementation units and DPR consultants to incorporate the new provisions in upcoming projects and ensure their adoption in ongoing projects wherever applicable. The revised policy supersedes the earlier toll plaza design guidelines for four-lane and wider highways, while two-lane highways with paved shoulders will continue under the existing tolling system.
Article Summary: NHAI has made Multi-Lane Free Flow (MLFF) tolling an integral part of highway development. The move will reduce land acquisition requirements and save public money. Electronic toll collection equipment will be mounted on overhead gantries instead of requiring multiple tolling lanes and booths.

Article Title: Tata Motors acquires majority stake in Italian commercial vehicle maker Iveco for 3.43 billion euros
Article Text:
Tata Motors announced Iveco deal in 2025.

NEW DELHI: Tata Motors on Friday acquired an 89.42% stake in Italian commercial vehicle maker Iveco Group for around 3.43 billion euros after the initial settlement of its cash tender offer, taking control of the European company as the acquisition process continues.The deal makes Iveco an indirect subsidiary of Tata Motors and marks the Indian automaker’s biggest acquisition since it bought Jaguar Land Rover from Ford in 2008. Iveco reported revenue of Rs 1,42,471 crore and employs around 33,000 people across 16 industrial sites and 22 research and development centres.In a joint statement on Friday, the companies said TML CV Holdings B.V., an indirect wholly owned subsidiary of Tata Motors, had acquired 238,157,212 common shares of Iveco, representing approximately 89.42% of its common share capital, excluding treasury shares.“Iveco Group has now become part of Tata Motors,” the company said, PTI reported. The settlement follows the completion of the acceptance period for Tata Motors’ voluntary cash tender offer, under which it offered 14.4 euros per share for Iveco’s common shares.The acceptance period will reopen for five trading days, from November 2 to November 6, 2026, giving shareholders another opportunity to tender their shares.The settlement for shares tendered during this period is scheduled for November 13.Tata Motors had initially offered 14.10 euros per share before raising the price by 0.30 euros to 14.40 euros, including dividends, on October 9.As part of the acquisition, Tata Sons chairman N Chandrasekaran has been appointed chairperson and senior non-executive director of Iveco. Olof Persson will continue as chief executive officer.Tata Motors executives P B Balaji and Girish Wagh have joined the board as non-independent, non-executive directors. Guenter Butschek and Charles Nichols have been appointed independent, non-executive directors.Iveco has also reconstituted its board committees, amended its corporate governance documents and repurchased all special voting shares.The companies said details of the next steps following the offer, including the voluntary purchase procedure, a Dutch-law squeeze-out process or a post-offer demerger and liquidation, would be communicated in due course.Tata Motors announced plans in 2025 to acquire Iveco, excluding its defence business, in a deal valued at around 3.8 billion euros (nearly Rs 38,240 crore). The transaction was to be carried out through TML CV Holdings Pte Ltd.The acquisition is aimed at expanding Tata Motors’ global commercial vehicle presence by combining its operations with Iveco’s established international network and product portfolio.
Article Summary: Tata Motors on Friday acquired an 89.42% stake in Italian commercial vehicle maker Iveco Group. The deal marks the Indian automaker’s biggest acquisition since it bought Jaguar Land Rover from Ford in 2008. The settlement follows the completion of the acceptance period for Tata Motors’ voluntary cash tender offer, under which it offered 14.4 euros per share.

Article Title: Zensar Q2 revenue rises 2%; AI-led deals account for 36% of order book
Article Text:
Zensar CEO Manish Tandon

BENGALURU: Mid-sized IT services firm Zensar Technologies reported a 2% year-on-year increase in revenue in constant currency terms, while sequential growth stood at 4.1%. in the September quarter. Its EBIT margin stood at 13.4%, down 30 basis points year-on-year.Banking and financial services was a key growth driver, with revenue in the vertical rising 17.1% year-on-year and 7.1% sequentially in constant currency terms. The US business grew 2.5% year-on-year, while Africa expanded 2.2%. Healthcare and life sciences declined 9.9%, and telecom, media and technology contracted 21.6% year-on-year in constant currency terms.AI-influenced deals accounted for 36% of the company’s order book in the quarter. CEO and managing director Manish Tandon said the company was seeing broad-based growth across verticals, except telecom. He said companies continuing to sell traditional services in traditional ways would find the market diminishing, while those taking newer offerings and concept-led solutions to customers would find opportunities.Tandon said around $30 million of deals were awaiting paperwork before being added to the order book, and he was not particularly concerned about the delay.On client expectations of productivity gains, he said IT services companies would increasingly have to move from time-and-materials contracts to outcome- and output-based models.He also believes AI is changing the industry’s talent requirements. “Writing code has become a commodity,” Tandon said, adding that companies would need engineers with deeper software engineering skills who could instruct AI tools to generate code, rather than those who merely write code quickly.Zensar’s headcount increased to 12,320, with 978 net additions during the quarter.
Article Summary: Mid-sized IT services firm Zensar Technologies reported a 2% year-on-year increase in revenue in constant currency terms. Banking and financial services was a key growth driver, with revenue in the vertical rising 17.1%. Healthcare and life sciences declined 9.9%, and telecom, media and technology contracted.

Article Title: DGCA nod: Air India becomes first Indian carrier to have its own flying school
Article Text:
AI Flying Academy will operate a fleet of 31 single-engine and three twin-engine aircraft for pilot training.

NEW DELHI: Air India has become the first Indian carrier to get the clearance to launch its own flying school. The Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) Friday approved Air India Flying Academy at Amravati’s Belora Airport in Maharashtra, strengthening pilot training capacity in India. AI Flying Academy will operate a fleet of 31 single-engine and three twin-engine aircraft for pilot training.Spread across 10 acres, the academy will feature digitally enabled classrooms, student accommodation, a digital operations centre, and a dedicated maintenance facility, providing aspiring pilots with world-class training infrastructure while maintaining the highest standards of safety and operational excellence.The Air India Flying Academy complements the airline’s commitment to developing aviation talent and infrastructure in India, including its 6 lakh square feet training academy in Gurugram, which is the largest aviation training institution in South Asia.Together, these investments are expected to support India’s growing demand for pilots and contribute to building a more self-reliant aviation ecosystem.AI said on X: “We are proud to receive DGCA approval for the Air India Flying Academy at Amravati's Belora Airport, making it the first flying academy established by an Indian airline in the country. ld-class training infrastructure and a planned fleet of 34 training aircraft, the academy will help strengthen India's pilot training capacity and support the nation's rapidly growing aviation sector.”
Article Summary: Air India has become the first Indian carrier to get the clearance to launch its own flying school. The Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) Friday approved Air India Flying Academy at Amravati’s Belora Airport. The academy will feature digitally enabled classrooms, student accommodation, a digital operations centre, and a dedicated maintenance facility.

Article Title: World's largest crypto exchange Binance probes 'security breach', $6.3 billion in assets impacted
Article Text:
Suspected hack hits world's largest crypto exchange Binance (Reuters photo)

Tether, Circle freeze funds linked to incident

Binance investigates possible access through employee laptop

According to Google Trends, searches for ‘binance hacked’ surged by over 5,000% in India in the past 24 hours.

Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, is investigating a potential security breach that could have affected assets worth around $6.3 billion, the company said on Thursday. However, it has not confirmed whether funds were stolen or established the full extent of the damage.Blockchain analysis firm TRM said North Korea was behind the $6 billion crypto hack on Binance.The exchange said it was working to resolve the issue and had temporarily suspended deposits and withdrawals while conducting security checks and coordinating with law enforcement and industry partners.“Rest assured that user funds are completely safe,” a Binance spokesperson said in a statement, adding that its security teams were reviewing all relevant information and would provide updates through official channels once the details were verified.In a post on X, Binance said its estimated total impact stood at around $6.3 billion, with roughly $3 billion in affected assets frozen on the blockchain so far. The company added that it was working with blockchain partners to trace and freeze additional funds.Binance's initial investigation suggested that the incident may have involved a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop, which allegedly allowed an attacker to access a service container and submit unauthorised withdrawal transactions.The exchange said it had found no evidence of a wallet private key leak. It added that further technical details would be released after the investigation was completed and the findings fully verified.Stablecoin issuers Tether and Circle have also frozen assets associated with the potential breach.Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino said the company had frozen more than $1.5 billion in assets linked to what he described as a potential Binance exchange hack. Circle co-founder and CEO Jeremy Allaire said the company had frozen more than $800 million in associated funds in coordination with law enforcement.Binance said it was working with law enforcement agencies, token issuers, blockchain intelligence firms and other industry partners to trace and freeze additional assets.Changpeng Zhao, Binance's founder who stepped down as CEO in 2023, also described the incident as a possible hack in a post on X.“User funds are safe!” Zhao wrote, adding that although he no longer managed Binance, he expected all user funds to be fully covered as a shareholder.The incident has also coincided with pressure on cryptocurrency markets. Bitcoin fell 3.2% on Thursday evening, slipping below $79,000.The suspected compromise of a DevOps engineer's laptop has emerged as a key line of inquiry. According to Binance's preliminary assessment, the attacker may have used access to a service container to initiate unauthorised withdrawals.The company has not confirmed the identity of the attacker or established whether the incident resulted in a loss of user funds. It said it would release more technical information after verifying the facts.The episode adds to persistent security concerns in the cryptocurrency industry, where exchanges and other platforms remain targets for cyberattacks and unauthorised transactions.Founded in 2017, Binance allows users to buy, sell and trade digital assets and has grown into the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange. Zhao stepped down as CEO in 2023 after pleading guilty to a felony related to failures to prevent money laundering on the platform. US President Donald Trump pardoned him in 2025.
Article Summary: Search for ‘binance hacked’ surged by over 5,000% in India in the past 24 hours. Tether, Circle freeze funds linked to incident. Binance investigates possible access through employee laptop. North Korea was behind the $6 billion crypto hack on Binance.

Article Title: Trump’s DHS hit by data breach as hackers expose records of 41,000 employees
Article Text:
The officers have faced scrutiny for wearing masks and sunglasses during operations and for failing to clearly identify themselves.

DHS acknowledges potential breach

More than 41,000 employees and contractors of the US department of homeland security (DHS), including thousands of immigration and border enforcement personnel, have had their work details exposed in a major data leak amid growing protests and criticism over President Donald Trump’s immigration crackdown.The officers have faced scrutiny for wearing masks and sunglasses during operations and for failing to clearly identify themselves.The leaked information includes names, work addresses, phone numbers and job descriptions of personnel working across several agencies, including Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and Customs and Border Protection (CBP), a BBC report reveals.The leaked records were published in a searchable online database called “Icepick” on Wednesday. The activist group department of peace said it accessed the information through a single sign-on service used by DHS employees, while cybersecurity researcher Maia Arson Crimew and the nonprofit Distributed Denial of Secrets helped make the data public.A DHS spokesperson said the department was “aware of a potential breach” and was working to address the situation. The spokesperson added that the agency takes security threats against its employees and officers seriously and would provide further updates when more information became available.According to the leaked data, more than 21,000 personnel listed work for CBP, while nearly 6,600 are associated with ICE. Other records reportedly cover employees of homeland security investigations, the federal protective service and the cybersecurity and infrastructure security agency.The groups behind the disclosure, however, said the database was not intended to be a comprehensive directory of all DHS employees. Rather the aim was to replace "anonymity with accountability", according to Emma Best, a co founder of DDoSecrets.
Article Summary: More than 41,000 employees and contractors of the US department of homeland security (DHS) have had their work details exposed in a major data leak. Leaked information includes names, work addresses, phone numbers and job descriptions of personnel working across several agencies. The officers have faced scrutiny for wearing masks and sunglasses during operations and for failing to clearly identify themselves.

Article Title: Wall Street reels from tech selloff as Nasdaq posts biggest single-day fall since June
Article Text:
In a surprising turn of events, US stocks experienced significant declines as Intel and Amazon reported disappointing earnings, casting doubt on artificial intelligence investments.

US stocks ended Friday's session with significant losses, as concerns over the scale of investments in artificial intelligence (AI) and the time required to generate returns weighed on investor sentiment. Disappointing quarterly performances from Intel and Amazon further fuelled the technology selloff, pushing the Nasdaq composite to its steepest single-day percentage decline since June 5, according to a Reuters report.The Nasdaq plunged 2.86 per cent to settle at 25,437.00, while the S&P 500 shed 1.82 per cent to close at 7,580.07. The Dow Jones Industrial Average also slipped 1.09 per cent, ending the session at 51,770.31.The technology-focused Nasdaq has now retreated 7.8 per cent from its record closing high registered on October 6. The latest wave of selling came after intel and amazon released their quarterly results late on Thursday, prompting investors to reassess the prospects of companies making substantial investments in AI.Intel shares suffered a steep 28.6 per cent decline, while other major chipmakers also witnessed heavy selling.Nvidia dropped 4.2 per cent and AMD lost 10.9 per cent. The broader semiconductor index tumbled 7.2 per cent, taking its monthly decline beyond 15 per cent.Server manufacturers were not spared either, with Dell shares falling 10.8 per cent and HP declining 9.6 per cent."It's fair to say that this week, not just today, has been very much about the future of AI and what that's going to look like, whether there will be a positive return on investment and if so, how quickly," Oliver Pursche, senior vice president at Wealthspire Advisors in New York, told Reuters.Pursche noted that companies delivering results in line with or above elevated market expectations were continuing to perform well, while those missing targets were facing significant selling pressure.The weakness extended beyond individual stocks. The S&P 500's broader technology sector registered its largest monthly percentage decline since March 2025. Meanwhile, the communication services sector recorded its sharpest monthly fall since April 2022.However, the overall corporate earnings picture remained encouraging despite the market downturn. According to LSEG data cited by reuters, 82 per cent of the 299 S&P 500 companies that had announced their third-quarter results had exceeded analysts' consensus estimates. Analysts had projected year-on-year earnings growth of 31.6 per cent for the quarter.Cryptocurrency-linked stocks also came under pressure following reports that hackers had stolen USD 6.3 billion from binance. Shares of coinbase, strategy and robinhood declined between 7.2 per cent and 10.6 per cent.According to the news agency ANI, All three key US stock indices ended the week in the red, with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq also posting losses for the month.
Article Summary: Nasdaq plunged 2.86 per cent to settle at 25,437.00, while the S&P 500 shed 1.82 per cent. Disappointing quarterly performances from Intel and Amazon further fuelled the technology selloff. The Nasdaq has now retreated 7.8 per cent from its record closing high registered on October 6.

Article Title: Google loses $500bn as China stocks suffer worst rout since 2016: What's happening to global AI?
Article Text:
Companies are increasingly turning to debt markets to finance the build-out

The bill is getting bigger, but where are the returns?

From chipmakers to China, the sell-off spreads

Investors are asking who can afford the AI race

For the past few years, artificial intelligence has been Wall Street's favourite investment story. Pour billions into chips, build data centres, promise a revolution and watch valuations soar. But the mood music is changing. Investors are beginning to ask an increasingly uncomfortable question: When, exactly, will all this spending start paying off?The answer is becoming more important as some of the biggest names in technology face a bruising week. Google's parent Alphabet suffered a record one-day fall, wiping more than $500 billion off its market value. Intel's shares plunged on a weak outlook, Amazon came under pressure over its spending and sales forecasts, while China's blue-chip stocks recorded their steepest monthly decline in more than a decade.From Silicon Valley to Shanghai, the AI trade is running into a reality check. So what's happening?Alphabet became the latest casualty after its third-quarter results disappointed investors. Its shares fell more than 12% on Thursday, their worst single-day percentage decline on record, wiping roughly $500 billion off its market capitalisation. The company's market value dropped from around $3.97 trillion to $3.46 trillion.The concerns went beyond a quarterly earnings miss. Alphabet reported revenue growth of 25% to $127.6 billion, but its advertising business failed to meet expectations. More significantly, executives acknowledged that Google's AI Mode was generating lower advertising monetisation than traditional search queries.Chief business officer Philipp Schindler said the strong growth in AI Mode queries had an impact because of the lower monetisation being seen. That admission raised a difficult question: Could Google's attempt to reinvent search with AI end up undermining the advertising business that finances much of its empire?The pressure is compounded by spending. Alphabet recorded $51.4 billion in capital expenditure in the third quarter alone and reported a second consecutive quarter of negative free cash flow. Microsoft, by comparison, generated $18.6 billion in free cash flow during the quarter despite its AI investments.Amazon has also faced scrutiny. Its shares fell after it offered a cautious sales forecast for the crucial holiday quarter. The company reported negative cash flow of $42 billion, reflecting the scale of its spending. Chief executive Andy Jassy defended the investment, arguing that cloud services, retail and its own chips could unlock enormous future opportunities.Microsoft has fared relatively better. Revenue rose 19% to $92.3 billion, while its cloud business grew 30% to $63 billion. Its results offered investors evidence that enterprise demand for AI remains strong, even as questions persist over where the technology's long-term value will ultimately accrue.Intel shares plunged more than 25% in premarket trading on Friday after the chipmaker forecast fourth-quarter revenue of $15 billion-$16 billion, below analysts' expectations of $17.07 billion. Its finance chief also said the company did not expect positive cash flow this year.The warning dragged semiconductor stocks lower, including Nvidia, AMD, Qualcomm and Broadcom. Server makers Dell, Hewlett Packard Enterprise and Super Micro Computer also fell, showing how the sell-off is spreading across the AI infrastructure supply chain.China's markets have taken an even harder hit. The CSI300 index fell 8.5% in October, its biggest monthly decline since early 2016, while the technology-focused STAR50 has lost around 40% in less than four months, according to Reuters. The correction has erased roughly $480 billion in market value from Chinese AI and semiconductor leaders.Chinese technology stocks had surged on expectations of strong domestic AI demand and Beijing's push for technological self-reliance. But high valuations, concerns over export restrictions and questions about future demand have undermined the rally. Some popular stocks, including robotics and chipmaking companies, have lost around half their value.The correction also highlights how heavily AI has come to dominate China's markets. Goldman Sachs estimates that AI-related stocks account for 42% of market capitalisation and 57% of turnover across mainland-listed and Hong Kong-listed shares.The scale of the investment explains the growing nervousness. Morgan Stanley expects spending on AI infrastructure to exceed $1 trillion next year. JP Morgan estimates global AI capital expenditure could reach $5.5 trillion by 2030, with $900 billion spent in 2026 alone.Companies are increasingly turning to debt markets to finance the build-out. Meta, Amazon and Alphabet have issued substantial amounts of bonds in recent years, while Microsoft is reportedly planning a $25 billion US investment-grade bond sale. Rising borrowing costs could make this strategy more expensive, particularly if AI revenues fail to keep pace.Investors are already reassessing their exposure. US equity funds recorded net outflows of $6.65 billion in the week ended October 28, their first weekly withdrawals in three weeks, according to LSEG Lipper data.
Article Summary: Companies are increasingly turning to debt markets to finance the build-out. Google's parent Alphabet suffered a record one-day fall, wiping more than $500 billion off its market value. Intel's shares plunged on a weak outlook, Amazon came under pressure over its spending and sales forecasts. China's blue-chip stocks recorded their steepest monthly decline in more than a decade.

Article Title: Big Tech's AI spending spree puts over $2 trillion in Nasdaq market value at risk
Article Text:
Nasdaq faces $2 trillion wipeout

Alphabet's record fall, Meta's fundraising plans add to concerns

Big Tech's rising debt adds to investor worries

Strong revenues offer support

AI spending reaches new highs

Over $2 trillion in market value is at risk for the tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 this month as investors question whether massive AI investments will pay off quickly enough.The possible loss would even be higher than SpaceX's entire market value.The index has already fallen more than 5.8% in October as concerns over the AI boom have weighed on technology stocks.
